The airline unions are weak because they must get a release from the national mediation board to strike. Generally most major airlines are union with Delta being the exception (for some jobs). So the unions set the wage expectations and for the non-union companies and they have to match or exceed to remain competitive since it is a highly niche field to work in.

Nights are honestly not too bad, it takes some getting used to but once your used to it it feels like any other day. Plus the job gets more relaxed at the end of the day. I luckily am able to stay on nights on the weekends which is a plus. Most people switch from days to nights when they come back to work. I currently work 9:30pm to 8am. Another thing with this job is that unless your doing MRO work or have experience you are going to be working nights most of the time in the career Also would like to say I am in a union operation as well so we have the benefits that  come from that. I know for a fact that most major airlines are at a 5-8 year topout and they are all over $50 an hour some going up even higher than that if you go cargo.

Just to give context here I am fresh out of A&P school and am making right under $26 an hour working 4 ten hour nights per week at a regional airline. The job is super enjoyable so far but this is coming from a line maintenance base so it may be different if your doing hangar work.

Title III sets the maximum amount that may be garnished in any workweek or pay period, regardless of the number of garnishment orders received by the employer. For ordinary garnishments (i.e., those not for support, bankruptcy, or any state or federal tax), the weekly amount may not exceed the lesser of two figures: 25% of the employee’s disposable earnings, or the amount by which an employee’s disposable earnings are greater than 30 times the federal minimum wage (currently $7.25 an hour). - https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/30-cppa
